name: Om'Mas Keith
notes: The Sa-Ra-lineage producer-engineer who bridges this lane and modern alt-R&B, **claimed here rather than in `trap-soul`** per the roadmap's fallback order, "because his harmonic idiom is neo-soul rather than 808-driven". `confidence` is **low** — the credits and the lineage are sourced, the parameters are inference from the records. The drums are the quietest thing on the record and the entry says so: "sparse and dry — a filtered kick on 1 and 3, a soft clap or rim on 2&4 mixed low, almost no hat carpet, and long fully drumless sections; where a break is used it is crushed and low-passed. **The kit is the least prominent element.**" That is a kick of 1–3 hits a bar on literal 1-and-3 anchors, a layered low-passed clap, a hat fill density of 0.06 and the softest velocity tiers in this producer batch. Harmony is "extension-heavy and modal — m9/maj9/13 voicings held over long static sections, chromatic side-slips, and abrupt unrelated-key sections inside one track. Written on keys" — `maxChords` 2, a triad weight of 0.03, 8-to-16-beat durations and a raised `susSubstitutionProb`. "Vocal production favours a single dry lead with wide, quiet stacks behind it", which is a low melodic density with a raised `emptyBarBias` and an octave-stacked counter at −12. The low end is "soft synth-sub or played bass with a long decay and minimal motion; slides are absent" — `mirror_kick` at a root probability of 0.9, deliberately **not** a `bass808` block, since a synth sub is not an 808 and authoring one would silence the bass part. ⚠ Every drum number and every melody figure here is INFERRED. ⚠ The suite/collage form — songs that change tempo or key mid-way — is not encodable and is carried only as very wide section-length ranges. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than the held `reese_sustain` the research describes** — *“soft synth-sub or played bass with a long decay and minimal motion; slides are absent.”* — and that is a limit of the engine rather than a reading of the record. `generators::phrase_spans` re-articulates a held span only when it runs longer than two bars, so over the four-bar clip `reese_sustain` writes at most four notes and cannot reach the 500-bassline floor `engine/tests/bass.rs` holds every model to. `mobb-deep`, `dmx` and `capone-n-noreaga` carry the same substitution for the same reason; `followRootsProb` stays where it was so the line still reads as roots under the chord. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 976/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** `melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.26 to 0.1. The counter's note count is `densityRatio` times the lead's own note count, so a bar the lead leaves empty is a bar the counter has nothing to answer — and one empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one, which is the single thing a seed cannot vary. Measured across this roster the models failing this gate average 0.150 here against 0.030 for the models that pass. ⚠ The value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "Rhodes/analog synth pads, live strings, and heavy use of found-sound, spoken-word and field-recording interludes as texture. Vocal production favours a single dry lead with wide, quiet stacks behind it.", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
